rationale: CoMD is a compute-dense molecular dynamics proxy app whose hot kernels (eamForce, ljForce, timestep, linkCells, haloExchange) dominate runtime, so the table favors cheap, low-risk passes applied broadly (SUB, SPLIT — the latter well suited to the large functions like printPerformanceResults at 4.4KB and main at 3.4KB) while giving FLA and BCF high SecurityGain/DiversityGain but steeply weighted RuntimeCost/SizeCost so the selector steers these expensive control-flow transforms toward cold-to-warm functions (parsers, YAML output, setup) rather than inner force-computation loops; IBR carries the strongest DiversityGain at moderate cost since indirect branching resists static CFG recovery without the loop-blunting effect of full flattening on hot kernels; ICALL aligns naturally with CoMD's existing function-pointer dispatch (lj/eam force selection) at low size cost; and IGV is included but with the highest CorrectnessRisk weight because CoMD's shared global state in parallel/communication paths (halo exchange, parallel.c) makes encoded-globals rewrites the most likely source of subtle breakage.
